groundings.excerpt:
922: We investigate further the situation when $W$ is a Weyl group of 
923: type $A_{n-1}$, which exhibits extra features; one can: 
924: \begin{enumerate}
925: \item[$\bullet$] be more explicit about bigrassmannians and their essential sets $\Ess(w)$,
926: \item[$\bullet$] produce even smaller generating sets for the ideals
927: $I_w$ and $J_v$, which are conjecturally minimal in the case of $J_v$, and
928: \item[$\bullet$] work with $\ZZ$ coefficients rather than
929: over a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero.

claims.text: Let \(A=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}A_d\) be a nonnegatively graded ring and \(F\) a homogeneous generating family of a nonzero graded ideal \(J\). If \(f\in F\) is nonzero and \(\deg g>\deg f\) for every \(g\in F\setminus\{f\}\), then \(f\) is indispensable: every element of the ideal generated by \(F\setminus\{f\}\) has zero degree-\(\deg f\) component.

For either family \[ \{\;s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\;\},\qquad \{\;s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\;\}, \] the member \(s_{i^j}\) is indispensable provided its image in \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\) is nonzero. Indeed, it has degree \(ij\), while every other indexed partition strictly contains \(i^j\) and hence has degree \(>ij\); apply the preceding claim.

If \[ a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)=0\quad\text{or}\quad b=\min(i,j)=0, \] then each displayed family is the singleton \(\{s_{i^j}\}\), since both upper bounding partitions equal \(i^j\). Consequently, under the accepted contextual assertion that these singleton families generate a nonzero \(J_v\), both are minimal.
